results.title: Cost of attendance | MIT Student Financial Services
results.snippet: The cost of attendance (COA) is our best estimate—based on defined costs set by MIT and surveys of our students—of what we expect it to cost an undergraduate to attend MIT for one academic year as a full-time student. ⁠It includes fixed costs that are billed by MIT (such as tuition, housing, food), and variable estimates for other expenses (such as books, supplies, and personal expenses).

results.title: Undergraduate Tuition & Aid – MIT Facts
results.snippet: The Institute’s generous financial aid program ensures that an MIT education is affordable for the most talented students in the world regardless of their family’s financial circumstances. MIT provides every undergraduate with sufficient financial aid to meet the difference (full need) between the MIT “sticker price” (the cost of attendance) and what their family can afford to pay (their demonstrated financial need).
